RubiQ-benchmark.ipynb (Colab, 2026-04-27): sweep.json, 36 runs = 6 methods x CIFAR-10 x alpha {0.1, 0.5} x 3 seeds, 30 rounds, warmup 5. mean_post_warmup: alpha 0.1 rubiq 0.2144 vs random_csi 0.2144 (delta 0.0000, CI [-0.0003, 0.0002], p 0.2695); alpha 0.5 rubiq 0.2807 vs random_csi 0.2813 (delta -0.0006, CI [-0.0011, -0.0003], p 0.0000). n_paired = 3 per cell.

The FL baselines are a parameter-matched MLP (775,369 params vs 775,626). scaffold sits at 0.1000 (chance) on every alpha-0.1 metric, so it did not train. RubiQ-vs-baseline deltas measure architecture and implementation, not the group. random_csi is the only group control, and it ties or slightly beats rubiq.

aggregate.py's docstring promises a per-class win count; the function body never computes it. The one-sided p is direction-matched (P(boot<=0) if delta>=0, else P(boot>=0)), so 'p 0.0000' at delta -0.0006 means random_csi > rubiq on that cell.
